classification.difficultyReason: Combines regular-polygon and isosceles-triangle angles to prove parallelism.

content.prompt: Prove that the red line segment shown below is parallel to the bottom side of the regular pentagon.

spec.description: Unlabelled pentagon with upward apex, horizontal bottom edge and red diagonal joining the upper-left and upper-right vertices. No equality or angle marks added.
spec.mathematics: Regularity is made explicit in the corrected prompt; prove the red diagonal parallel to the bottom side.
spec.answerVisibility: No numerical angles or proof supplied.

answer.short:
The red segment is parallel to the bottom side.

Its co-interior angles with the bottom side are $72^{\circ}$ and $108^{\circ}$, which sum to $180^{\circ}$.
answer.worked:
Label the upper-left, top, upper-right, bottom-right and bottom-left vertices $A,B,C,D,E$, respectively. Each interior angle of the regular pentagon is
$$\frac{(5-2)\times180^{\circ}}{5}=108^{\circ}.$$
Since $AB=BC$, triangle $ABC$ is isosceles.
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAC&=\frac{180^{\circ}-108^{\circ}}{2}\\\angle BAC&=36^{\circ}\\\angle CAE&=108^{\circ}-36^{\circ}\\\angle CAE&=72^{\circ}\\\angle CAE+\angle DEA&=72^{\circ}+108^{\circ}\\\angle CAE+\angle DEA&=180^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The co-interior angles are supplementary, so $AC\parallel DE$.
